---
title: "Bind each column once in SQLite upserts on D1"
description: "Drop when the pinned release contains PR 18239 or another fix that binds each column of a SQLite upsert once on D1."
---

<!-- Generated by `pnpm upstream export` from the patch's commit message on top of Payload v4.0.0-beta.2. Edit the commit, not this page. -->

On D1, updating a document whose main table has more than 50 columns fails
with "D1_ERROR: too many SQL variables". upsertRow saves an update as
INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET, which binds every column twice, once in
VALUES and once in SET. D1 accepts at most 100 bound parameters per statement.
An upload collection with seven image variants has 80 columns, so editors
can't change a media item's alt text, focal point or folder.

When the adapter sets limitedBoundParameters, as the D1 adapter does, SET now
reads each value it repeats from SQLite's excluded row, so the statement binds
each column once. D1 allows at most 100 columns per table, so an upsert stays
within the limit. The exception is an update with a where condition on a
table at that column limit, because the condition binds its own values.
Postgres and the other SQLite adapters build the same statement as before.

- **Patch:** `d1-upsert-bound-parameters`, committed as `fix(drizzle): bind each column once in SQLite upserts on D1`
- **Upstream:** [payloadcms/payload#18239](https://github.com/payloadcms/payload/pull/18239)
- **Tests:** `pnpm exec vitest run --project unit packages/drizzle/src/sqlite/insert.spec.ts; e2e suite (media update and delete test)`
